headline: Elevated, rising: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, which is likely to push fuel prices up next week.
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two to three oil tankers hit sea mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz today; this is Iran's account, reported widely by news agencies, and damage is not yet independently confirmed. Oil markets are closed for the weekend, so any price jump would show from Monday and reach SA bowsers within days. The US nationwide flight halt has ended; officials blame old, overloaded air-traffic communications equipment and say it was not a cyber attack. Locally: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no fire bans or CFS warnings, and the grid and phone networks are normal.
actions: Top up the car (and any generator fuel) this weekend before any Monday oil-price rise reaches SA bowsers.
If anyone is flying to or through the US in the next few days, check the airline app: delays are still clearing after the nationwide ground stop.
Check your bushfire plan and CFS app watch zones as Fire Danger Seasons start across SA.

categories.name: Geopolitical & conflict
categories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers that 'violated' their rules hit mines and caught fire in Hormuz, a new step after the reported strike on Sirik on 12 November. The US says its blockade of Iran will continue indefinitely. GPS-jamming flags over the Gulf and Israel this morning have eased back to normal; Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no warning signs and forecast markets are flat.

sources.title: The Star (Reuters): Iran's IRGC says two tankers hit sea mines in Hormuz
Xinhua: IRGC says 2 'violating' tankers caught fire after hitting mines

categories.name: Nuclear & fallout
categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal and no private jets are heading to retreat destinations. Iran's talk of leaving the nuclear treaty raises long-run risk, but there is no sign of any nuclear alert.

sources.title: Fox News: Tehran weighs nuclear treaty exit

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure
categories.summary: The US nationwide flight halt lasted about four and a half hours; US officials blame overloaded, outdated air-traffic communications equipment and Homeland Security says it was not a cyber attack. Microsoft 365 has recovered and Microsoft also ruled out an attack. Australian phone carriers and the SA grid are normal and the global threat level is green.

sources.title: ABC7: Nationwide ground stop lifted after more than 4 hours, old overloaded tech blamed
MS NOW: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after more than four hours

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: WHO reports two confirmed MERS cases in Qatar (MERS spreads person to person only with close contact) and the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria, with no cases outside Africa. The lit 'chemical attack' sign is a historical Syria story. Adelaide emergency departments are normal.

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges today and tomorrow and no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or severe-weather warnings. A strong wind warning is out for Spencer Gulf on Sunday. Six small fires active across SA; several outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz still carries only about 4 ships a day (100+ before the war) and the reported mine strikes make the few remaining passages riskier. Brent closed the week at about US$95.80 and the dollar is near 67.7 US cents; any oil jump would show when markets reopen Monday. Australia remains at Level 2 of the National Fuel Security Plan; Malacca, Lombok, Sunda and Torres routes are normal.

sources.title: gCaptain: Iran says LNG tanker hit mine in Hormuz

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Brent US$95.84 (flat), VIX 19.3 (+3%), gold US$3,886 (flat), AUD 0.677 (-0.5%). Markets were calm at Friday's close, but the Hormuz mine reports came after it, so oil and the dollar may move on Monday.

concerns.title: Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz shipping
drivers: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two to three tankers hit sea mines and caught fire in Hormuz today; this is Iran's claim, carried by Reuters and Xinhua, and the ships' identity and damage are not yet independently confirmed.

The US says its blockade of Iran will continue indefinitely and its new task force is targeting Iran's land supply routes; no new US strikes are confirmed since the reported hit on Sirik on 12 November.
Hormuz still carries only about 4 ships a day; forecast markets give about 21% for a Hormuz deal by year end.

scenarios.name: Standoff drags on with mine and ship incidents
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices stay high and may jump next week; occasional regional servo shortages but no rationing.

scenarios.name: Deal reached, shipping recovers
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel prices ease over weeks; little direct effect on SA.

scenarios.name: Major escalation: renewed US/Israeli strike campaign or wider Gulf attacks
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel price jump and local shortages within 1-3 weeks; possible government fuel measures.

actions.action: Top up the car and any generator fuel this weekend.
actions.reason: Oil markets reopen Monday; price rises reach SA bowsers within days, and a full tank avoids buying at the peak or during panic buying.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home.
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

concerns.title: Cyber attacks and outages hitting Australian services
drivers: Microsoft 365 has recovered and Microsoft ruled out an attack; the US flight halt was blamed on old, overloaded communications equipment, not hackers.
All Australian phone carriers are normal, the global threat level is green and exploited-flaw counts are only slightly above usual, though a Check Point firewall flaw is being actively exploited.

scenarios.name: Ongoing breaches and occasional cloud outages
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of disruption to email and online services; scam risk from stolen data.

scenarios.name: Hours-long outage of payments or a telco
scenarios.sa_impact: Card payments and phones down for hours.

scenarios.name: Multi-day multi-sector attack
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, fuel and communications disrupted for days.

actions.action: Keep devices and banking apps updated.
actions.reason: Most attacks on households exploit known flaws that updates already fix.

concerns.title: Local SA emergency (bushfire, heat, power) within 7 days
drivers: Fire danger is Moderate in the Hills and there is no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or severe-weather warnings, and six small fires active across SA.
A strong wind warning is out for Spencer Gulf for Sunday; the SA grid is normal and the flood road closures are in the far north-east, well away from Adelaide.

scenarios.name: Quiet week
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Hot, windy day with fire bans
scenarios.sa_impact: Fire danger High to Extreme in the Hills; travel plans may need changing.

scenarios.name: Damaging fire or major power outage
scenarios.sa_impact: Evacuations, power and phone outages in affected areas.

actions.action: Check your bushfire plan and the CFS app alert zones before the first hot spell.
actions.reason: Early-season fires start fast, and decisions are easier made on a calm day.

concerns.title: AI-enabled attack (non-traditional)
drivers: Reports of an AI-driven cyber attack on a European telecom and AI-assisted fraud in India; none targeting Australia.
A central bank overseas warned of deepfake videos of its governor; the Microsoft and US flight outages were both officially ruled not to be attacks.

scenarios.name: Background AI-assisted crime and espionage
scenarios.sa_impact: More convincing scams and data breaches; no wide outage.

scenarios.name: Synthetic-media crisis (fake leader video or alert)
scenarios.sa_impact: Hours of confusion, possible panic buying before it is debunked.

scenarios.name: Machine-speed attack on many systems at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Payments, telcos, hospitals or the grid disrupted for hours to days.

actions.action: Agree a family code word for urgent calls.
actions.reason: AI can clone a voice from seconds of audio; a code word defeats fake 'I need help now' calls.

concerns.title: Taiwan Strait pressure
drivers: Chinese navy drills in the Western Pacific and combat patrols continue; this is pressure, not a blockade.
No live-fire warnings, GPS jamming or internet disruption around Taiwan; Taiwan Strait shipping is normal and forecast markets give about 3% for a clash before 2027.

scenarios.name: Routine grey-zone pressure
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.name: Large announced drill
scenarios.sa_impact: Market jitters; no supply effect.

scenarios.name: Blockade or quarantine
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel, medicine and electronics disruption within weeks.

actions.action: Keep 2-3 months of any essential prescription medicines.
actions.reason: Most medicines are imported via Asian shipping lanes, which any blockade would disrupt first.

concerns.title: Ebola in Africa and MERS in the Gulf
drivers: WHO reports the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continuing in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria, with no cases outside Africa.
WHO also reports two confirmed MERS cases in Qatar; MERS spreads between people only through close contact, mostly in hospitals. Adelaide emergency departments are normal.

scenarios.name: Outbreaks stay contained in their regions
scenarios.sa_impact: No direct effect; possible extra airport screening.

scenarios.name: Isolated imported case in a Western country
scenarios.sa_impact: Media concern; Australian hospitals manage under existing plans.

scenarios.name: Spread in Asia-Pacific
scenarios.sa_impact: Travel restrictions and health system alerts.

actions.action: Check Smartraveller before any travel to Central or East Africa or the Gulf.
actions.reason: Advice and entry rules can change quickly as outbreaks and the conflict develop.

concerns.title: Undersea cables and Australian networks
drivers: No foreign vessels are on the cable watch list near Australia this run and all Australian carriers are normal.
This morning's 'military aircraft going dark' flag over Australia was not backed by any report and looks like a tracking gap; no undersea cable damage reported near Australia.

scenarios.name: Routine shipping, no damage
scenarios.sa_impact: No effect.

scenarios.sa_impact: Slower international internet for days; traffic reroutes via other cables.

scenarios.name: Several cables cut at once
scenarios.sa_impact: Major internet, payments and cloud disruption across Australia.

actions.reason: EFTPOS and card payments are the first thing to fail in a network outage.
